title: OmniMem: Scalable and Adaptive Memory Retrieval for Long Video Generation
claim: Combining local, compressed and sparsely selected long-range memory branches, with window exclusion and shared selection, gives scalable, efficient access to a growing history.
layout: Left main pipeline flowing top-to-bottom, right column of zoomed detail panels in dashed callout
description: A two-part architecture diagram. On the left, a rounded box shows the full-resolution KV cache as a row of 2x2 chunk icons shaded from dark orange (older) to pale (recent). Arrows lead down into three branches: Sliding Window, Compression (pooled KV blocks) and Selection (Top-K). Each branch feeds an attention block (Sliding-Window, Compression, Selection Attention). Current chunk queries join them, and gated multiplication circles (g^swa, g^cmp, g^slc) merge the outputs into a Gated Output. The Selection branch is outlined with a dashed blue box and linked by dashed lines to enlarged panels on the right. Those panels cover Adaptive Window Exclusion, Query-Shared KV Selection, Per-Head Scattered KV Access, and On-Demand KV Residency with GPU hot and CPU offload caches. Orange gradients carry the eye through the flow.
caption: Overview of OmniMem. Current-chunk queries attend to recent KV blocks, pooled historical KV blocks, and retrieved full-resolution KV blocks through sliding-window, compression, and selection attention, respectively. The right panels summarize the key retrieval and access designs: filtering near-window candidates before Top-K selection, sharing Top-K selection within query groups, and accessing per-head block slots with on-demand GPU residency.
abstract: Autoregressive (AR) video generation extends videos by producing latent chunks sequentially, but scaling to long videos requires repeated access to a growing historical KV cache. Existing methods reduce this cost by truncating the KV cache or compressing it into implicit memory, but both lose explicit access to query-relevant historical details. We propose OmniMem, an explicit full-range memory retrieval framework that performs sparse KV retrieval over the historical cache. To make this practical for chunk-based AR video generation, OmniMem addresses two issues: (i) local bias in sparse KV selection and (ii) Union Explosion in memory access. Adaptive Window Exclusion removes local-window blocks from the selection candidates when sufficient long-range history is available, preserving the sparse budget for informative long-range retrieval. Query-Shared KV Selection reduces cross-query diversity, while Per-Head Scattered KV Access avoids expanding head-specific selections into a large selected KV buffer. This allows each attention head to retrieve non-contiguous KV blocks according to its own selection pattern. Experiments on long-video generation show that OmniMem improves Dynamic Degree by 52.3% and preserves strong consistency over strong baselines, while maintaining comparable memory usage.
